field: detailedAnalysis[1].content[1] ("When Does Damage Extent Favor Roof Replacement?", paragraph 2)
quote: **Roof replacement** also turns cost-effective under the widely cited "50% rule" — one repair exceeding 50% of replacement cost leans to replace — and the "30% rule," where repair approaching 30% of replacement cost leans the same way, per WeatherShield, Home Depot, and Modernize industry consensus.
issue: Wrong-source / over-attribution. The trailing "per WeatherShield, Home Depot, and Modernize industry consensus" attaches all three sources jointly to BOTH the 50% rule and the 30% rule, but the canonical pack table pins them oppositely: facts-materials-economics.md §8 line 305 sources the 50% rule to "WeatherShield / Home Depot / industry" (Modernize NOT listed), and line 306 sources the 30% rule to "Kellow / Modernize / Josten (NJ)" (WeatherShield and Home Depot NOT listed). So Modernize does not back the 50% rule, and WeatherShield/Home Depot do not back the 30% rule. The page's own FAQ2 (faqs[1]) already splits these correctly — "per WeatherShield and Home Depot; a related '30% rule'... per Kellow Construction and Modernize" — so this body sentence is also internally inconsistent with the page.
fix: Replace "leans the same way, per WeatherShield, Home Depot, and Modernize industry consensus." with "leans the same way — the 50% rule per WeatherShield and Home Depot, the 30% rule per Kellow Construction and Modernize." (Re-pins each rule to its actual pack source and aligns with FAQ2.)
refuteReason: Confirmed against facts-materials-economics.md §8: line 305 (50% rule = WeatherShield / Home Depot / industry) and line 306 (30% rule = Kellow / Modernize / Josten NJ). Modernize is absent from line 305 and WeatherShield/Home Depot are absent from line 306, so the jointed trailing attribution mis-pins sources. Ruleset R7/R10 require each point's named authority to be the one that actually backs it; the page's own FAQ2 attributes these correctly, making the body sentence internally inconsistent. Not a false positive.

field: detailedAnalysis[1].content[0] ("When Does Damage Extent Favor Roof Replacement?", lead)
quote: the "25% rule" and "30% rule" are contractor rules of thumb, per RapidRestore and NJ contractor Josten Roofing, not code
issue: Loose joint attribution. The pack sources the damage-AREA "25% rule" to RapidRestore / MyQuoteIQ (facts-materials-economics.md §8 line 307) and the cost-ratio "30% rule" to Kellow / Modernize / Josten NJ (line 306; Josten's 30–40% NJ framing also at line 279). Pairing both rules jointly to "RapidRestore and Josten Roofing" implies each source backs both rules; per the pack RapidRestore backs only the 25% (area) rule and Josten backs only the 30% (cost-ratio) framing. Both named sources are genuinely in the packs and the "not code" framing is correct (it properly separates these rules of thumb from the unrelated N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 25%-permit trigger), so this is a precision defect, not a fabrication.
fix: Replace "the \"25% rule\" and \"30% rule\" are contractor rules of thumb, per RapidRestore and NJ contractor Josten Roofing, not code" with "the \"25% rule\" (damage area, per RapidRestore) and \"30% rule\" (repair cost share, per NJ contractor Josten Roofing) are contractor rules of thumb, not code". Pins each rule to its real pack source and removes the implied cross-backing.
refuteReason: Confirmed against facts-materials-economics.md §8: line 307 (25% rule, damage area = RapidRestore / MyQuoteIQ) and line 306/line 279 (30% rule, cost ratio = Kellow / Modernize / Josten NJ). The pack supports RapidRestore for the area rule and Josten for the cost-ratio rule only — neither source backs the other rule — so the jointed pairing over-attributes. Both sources do appear in the packs and "not code" is correct (distinct from the N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 permit trigger), so it is a real low-severity precision fix, not a refutable false positive.
